title: Skin care for eczema
intro: Atopic eczema makes the skin dry, itchy and prone to inflammation. Daily skin care with moisturisers is the foundation of treatment, reducing flare-ups and the need for medicated creams. A consistent routine, gentle products and trigger avoidance make a real difference.

sections.heading: Why skin care matters
paragraphs: In eczema, the skin barrier is impaired, so skin loses moisture and allows irritants and allergens to enter. This causes dryness, itching and inflammation. Regularly restoring the barrier reduces symptoms and can lengthen the time between flares.

sections.heading: Moisturising
paragraphs: Apply an emollient generously at least once or twice a day, and more in dry weather, ideally straight after bathing while skin is still slightly damp. Ointments and thick creams are more effective than light lotions, though the best product is one you will use. Apply downward in the direction of hair growth, and use plenty, as a lot is needed for the whole body.

sections.heading: Bathing and washing
paragraphs: Short lukewarm baths or showers of about five to ten minutes are fine. Use soap-free, fragrance-free cleansers, and pat the skin dry instead of rubbing. Bath oils can help but make the bath slippery. Avoid long hot baths, bubble baths and harsh soaps.

sections.heading: Clothing and triggers
paragraphs: Choose soft, breathable fabrics such as cotton, and avoid wool and rough seams. Wash clothes in mild detergent and rinse well. Keep fingernails short to limit scratching damage, and use cotton gloves at night if needed. Triggers vary and may include sweating, heat, dust, pets, stress and certain skin products. Identify and limit your own.

sections.heading: Managing flares and itching
paragraphs: During a flare, use the anti-inflammatory creams prescribed by your doctor in addition to emollients, as directed. Cool compresses, wet wraps and distraction help with itching. Seek advice if skin looks infected, with weeping, crusting or fever, or if sleep and daily life are badly affected. Children with eczema benefit from a routine that is calm and consistent.

examples.title: Building a routine
examples.text: Imagine your child has dry itchy skin. You could moisturise after the bath and again before bed, use a fragrance-free cleanser and keep a small tube in the school bag for dry spells.

examples.title: Choosing products
examples.text: Suppose a new lotion stings. You might stop using it, return to a plain emollient and ask your doctor or pharmacist for a gentle alternative.
